nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management)

medications.dose: 1.25 mg orally once daily (start); titrate by 1.25 mg every 2–4 weeks to max 5 mg daily as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong — review BP and serum K⁺/creatinine after 1–2 weeks, then titrate; aim BP <130/80 mmHg
medications.purpose: Reduce proteinuria and slow CKD progression; control hypertension
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends ACE‑I/ARB for CKD with ACR ≥30 mg/mmol or hypertension; monitor creatinine and potassium after 1–2 weeks

medications.dose: 20 mg orally once daily in the evening
medications.duration: Lifelong — review lipid profile annually and assess for side‑effects
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction in CKD (risk‑equivalent status)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 states all CKD patients should receive a statin for CV risk reduction

contraindications.reason: eGFR 10.8 mL/min/1.73 m² is below the NICE threshold (≥20 mL/min) for use
contraindications.alternative: Do not prescribe; focus on ACE‑I and statin

contraindications.reason: eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² – risk of lactic acidosis
contraindications.alternative: Discontinue if present; consider insulin therapy for glycaemic control

contraindications.reason: Accelerate CKD progression and cause fluid retention; contraindicated in CKD‑5
contraindications.alternative: Use acetaminophen for pain if needed

contraindications.drug: ARB (e.g., Losartan) in combination with ACE‑I
contraindications.reason: Dual RAAS blockade increases risk of hyperkalaemia and AKI (NG203 contraindication)
contraindications.alternative: Use ACE‑I alone; add other antihypertensives only if BP remains uncontrolled

contraindications.reason: eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² – high risk of contrast‑induced nephropathy
contraindications.alternative: Avoid unless essential; if required, pre‑hydrate and involve nephrology

assumptions_warnings: Current blood pressure reading not provided – assumed above target; will measure before titration.
Baseline serum potassium and liver function tests not available – order before initiating ramipril and atorvastatin.
Allergy status unknown – verify no ACE‑I or statin hypersensitivity before prescribing.
Diabetes regimen not detailed – assume patient is on insulin; avoid metformin per eGFR.
Patient’s use of over‑the‑counter medications not recorded – counsel to avoid NSAIDs.
treatment_summary: Start ramipril 1.25 mg daily (titrate to 5 mg) to control hypertension and reduce proteinuria, and atorvastatin 20 mg nightly for cardiovascular risk reduction. Monitor BP, serum potassium, creatinine, and liver enzymes after 1–2 weeks, then regularly. Avoid SGLT2 inhibitors, metformin, chronic NSAIDs, and ACE‑I/ARB combination due to severe CKD. Provide lifestyle advice (low‑salt diet, smoking cessation, weight management) and arrange baseline labs and follow‑up as per NICE NG203.
